title: What comes next in these four multiplication patterns?
description: Four boxes of multiplications are worked out line by line, the digits are read for a pattern, and each box is extended by one more line. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the digits keep climbing past five.
teaching_notes: One idea: work out the given lines, read the digits for the pattern, and then check the digit count of the next line. Ask the class what they notice in the first two lines of one box before the third line is shown. Watch for students who keep a pattern going without checking how many digits the product can have.

source: In each of the following boxes, the multiplications produce interesting patterns. Evaluate them to find the pattern. Extend the multiplications based on the observed pattern.
video_script.why: The child multiplies large numbers, and now reads the digits of the products for a pattern and extends it.
video_script.substitution: Work out each given line, name the pattern in the digits, write the next line, and check its digit count.
video_script.anchor: Four boxes of multiplications: 11 × 11 and two more, 66 × 61 and two more, 3 × 5 and two more, 101 × 101 and two more.
video_script.wrong_answer: one two three four five six five four three two one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko keeps climbing to six after the five. Five ones times five ones is less than ten digits long, and 12345654321 has eleven digits.
video_script.payoff_line: Each box extends by reading its digits

final_answer.spoken: one two three four five four three two one; four four four four zero two two two two six; one one one one five five five five; ten thousand eight hundred sixteen

never_show: a next line before the answer beat
maths_rules: a 5-digit number times a 5-digit number has at most 10 digits, so a product with 11 digits is wrong
video_script.design: One idea: work out the lines, read the digits for the pattern, check the digit count. Wrong idea: Keeko says the digits keep climbing past five. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>Then we read the digits of the answers and predict the next line.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 11 × 11 = 121; 111 × 111 = 12,321; 1111 × 1111 = 12,34,321; the digits climb to the number of ones, then fall back; five ones climb only to 5

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first box gives one two one, and then one two three two one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The third line is one two three four three two one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The digits climb up to the number of ones, and fall back.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Five ones will climb only up to five.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the second box gives four zero two six, and then four four zero two two six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The third line is four four four zero two two two six.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The pattern is a run of fours, a zero, a run of twos, and a six. The runs grow by one each time.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 3 × 5 = 15; 33 × 35 = 1155; 333 × 335 = 1,11,555; as many 1s as 5s, one more of each every line

marks.m3: the 1s and the 5s are counted and matched

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the third box gives one five, and then one one five five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The third line is one one one five five five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each line has as many ones as fives, and one more of each than before.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 101 × 101 = 10,201; 102 × 102 = 10,404; 103 × 103 = 10,609; split as 1 | middle pair | end pair; for 104: middle 08, end 16
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, the last box gives one zero two zero one, and then one zero four zero four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The third line is one zero six zero nine.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The middle pair goes up by two each time, and the end pair is one, four, nine.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The next line has a middle pair of eight and an end pair of sixteen.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the next product is one two three four five six five four three two one. The digits seem to keep climbing.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But a number with five digits times a number with five digits has at most ten digits.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That slip has eleven digits, so it cannot be right.
